findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Set/Image.lean:270 `theorem image_inter ... : f '' (s ∩ t) = f '' s ∩ f '' t`
findings.fix: Flip the statement to `sweep (P ∩ Q) n = sweep P n ∩ sweep Q n`, matching `Set.sweep_iUnion` in the same file, or rename it `sweep_inter_sweep`.
findings.issue: `Set.sweep_inter` proves `sweep P n ∩ sweep Q n = sweep (P ∩ Q) n`. That is the reverse of the Mathlib convention in which `image_inter` has `f '' (s ∩ t)` on the left. Code that pattern-matches `image_inter` will rewrite the wrong way.
`Set.finrank_sweep` is about `Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ (sweep P n))`, but the name leaves out `vectorSpan`. A set has no `finrank`, so the name does not describe the conclusion.

findings.evidence: The naming conventions' symbol dictionary gives `+` → `add` and `•` → `smul`; the conclusion is read outward from the term.
findings.fix: Rename it `add_smul_notMem_sweep`, describing the conclusion with the standard symbol names `add` and `smul`.
findings.issue: `Set.positive_translate_notMem_sweep` uses the prose words 'positive translate'. Its conclusion is `x + t • n ∉ sweep P n`.

findings.evidence: The 'Predicates as suffixes' section says `_surjective` is used for `Surjective f`; compare `Set.image_surjective` (Data/Set/Image.lean:1318).
findings.issue: `ContinuousLinearMap.surjective_smul_add_sweepProjection` puts `surjective` first. Mathlib writes `_surjective` as a suffix.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Set/Image.lean:395 `theorem Nonempty.image (f : α → β) {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty → (f '' s).Nonempty`
findings.fix: Rename it `Set.Nonempty.sweep` so that `hP.sweep n` works.
findings.issue: `Set.sweep_nonempty (hP : P.Nonempty) (n)` takes a `Set.Nonempty` proof as its first explicit argument, so it belongs in that namespace. Mathlib states the analogous fact as `Set.Nonempty.image`.

summary: Three names misdescribe their conclusions (`sweep_inter`, `finrank_sweep`, `positive_translate_notMem_sweep`), and two break Mathlib conventions (the `surjective_` prefix and `sweep_nonempty`, which should use dot notation).
